supporting_question.question: Damage to which nerve results in a 'claw hand' deformity due to loss of innervation to the medial lumbricals?
supporting_question.explanation: The ulnar nerve innervates the medial two lumbricals. Damage to this nerve leads to the characteristic 'claw hand' deformity (hyperextension at the metacarpophalangeal joints and flexion at the interphalangeal joints of the 4th and 5th digits).

true_false.statement: The ulnar nerve passes posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus.
true_false.explanation: The ulnar nerve runs in the cubital tunnel posterior to the medial epicondyle, where it is vulnerable to compression or injury.
